newsitem.title: USA: U.S corp debt issuers batter up amid drop in rates.
newsitem.headline: U.S corp debt issuers batter up amid drop in rates.

text.p: Corporate bond issuers, currently warming up in the primary bull pen, are getting set to pitch some deals amid Wednesday's drop in long-term interest rates, dealers said.
Earlier, benign reports on U.S. wholesale inflation and retail sales triggered the benchmark 30-year long bond to rise over a point, sending the yield down to 6.57 percent.
"At these levels you'll see those issuers who have been contemplating issuance step up to the plate," said one high-grade syndicate source.
On Wednesday, the government reported July Producer Price Index fell 0.1 percent overall and 0.1 percent excluding food and energy, indicating no signs of inflationary pressures.
In addition, July retail sales came in slightly more moderate than expected, with a rise of 0.6 percent versus a consensus forecast of up 0.7 percent.

Meanwhile, among high-grade deals expected to come on Wednesday are Texas Utilities' $300 million Baa2/BBB 10-year debt offering via Morgan Stanley Dean Witter. Price talk on the issue is seen between 75 - 80 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
Another issuer, ServiceMaster Co LP, is expected to issue a $300 million two-part debt offering via JP Morgan Securities.

ServiceMaster's deal is expected to include $150 million in 10-year debt and $150 million in 30-year debt. Proceeds from the offering will be used to reduce borrowings under bank credit facilities, the firm said.
ServiceMaster provides management of housekeeping, plant operations, food, linen and other services to healthcare and educational facilities.

Price talk for the $350 million cash-pay tranche is 8.75-9.0 percent, while price talk on the $250 million (proceeds) zero coupon tranche is seen between 75-87.5 basis points over over the cash-pay notes, sources said.
Merrill Lynch & Co, the lead underwriter, is expected to price the deal on Thursday.
Elsewhere, Central European Media Enterprises Ltd, restructured its upcoming junk offering to include a mark denominated tranche.
The offering originally consisted of $125 million in seven-year senior notes.
The deal, rated B1/B-plus, is expected to be priced via Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter, Discover & Co on Thursday.

Among other junk deals expected this week are: Burke Industries' $100 million 144a issue via Nationsbanc, Capstar Hotel's $150 million 10-year 144a issue via Lehman Brothers, Tricom SA's $165 million 144a seven-year notes via Bear Stearns, Dailey Petroleum Services' $100 million 144a issue via Jeffries & Co and Southern Food Group's $150 million 10-year note deal via Chase Securities.
